title: Accelerate-to-Demonstrate (A2D) Facility
summary: Grants of US$1–5 million for large-scale demonstration of proven clean-energy and industrial-decarbonisation technologies in developing countries. Its 2026 call included recovery and recycling of critical minerals.
objectives: Support projects that demonstrate proven technologies at industrial scale and can be scaled and commercialised.
mineralScope: Under the 2026 call's critical-minerals theme: low-carbon recovery and recycling of critical minerals from waste streams, decarbonising processing, refining and transport, and supply-chain optimisation.
period: Activities must be completed by 14 December 2030.
applicants: Businesses with innovations that can deliver real-world emissions reductions in developing countries. Full criteria are on UNIDO's procurement portal, which we have not read.
exclusions: Projects at the planning stage, research and development, or early-stage pilot testing.
accessRoute: Calls run through UNIDO's procurement portal. The 2026 call closed on 18 June 2026.
whyItMatters: A rare grant source that names critical-mineral recycling and processing, for technology demonstration at industrial scale.
notEstablished: It is not a source for community organising, rights work or small projects. We have not seen the list of awarded projects.

passages.quote: Low‑carbon solutions to recover and recycle critical minerals from waste streams
A2D does not support projects at the planning stage, research and development, or early‑stage pilot testing.
All supported activities must be completed no later than 14 December 2030.

title: Fair Focus on Trade (FFT)
summary: Dutch subsidy programme for civil-society organisations working on clean and fair trade in value chains important to the Netherlands, including mining and critical raw materials. Closed in August 2026 and will not reopen.
geography: 21 listed countries in Africa and Asia
objectives: Strengthen civil-society organisations through capacity strengthening, service provision, dialogue and financing of in-country partners, to make value chains more sustainable.
mineralScope: Mining and critical raw materials was one of three eligible sectors, alongside agriculture and agri-food, and garments and textiles.
period: Five-year projects (60 months), with a six-month inception phase.
applicants: Civil-society organisations with a legal establishment in the Netherlands or a target country, at least five years of relevant experience in the same country and value chain, and other threshold criteria.
exclusions: For-profit organisations; government or majority government-owned organisations; intergovernmental organisations; applications made as or on behalf of a partnership such as an alliance or consortium.
accessRoute: None. The source says the programme is closed and will not reopen.
whyItMatters: A worked example of how a donor writes eligibility for civil-society mineral work: single applicant, track record in the same country and value chain, and all four activity types combined.
notEstablished: Which projects were selected, and whether any concern mining in India or Indonesia, is not recorded here.

passages.quote: This subsidy is closed. You can no longer apply for this programme. It will not reopen.
Each selected project can receive between 10 and 22 million euros. We will select a maximum of 8 projects.

title: Dutch Diamonds Partnerships (DDP)
summary: Dutch subsidy programme for public-private partnerships on water security, food security and sustainable market development in low- and middle-income countries. Minerals are not a named theme.
objectives: Sustainable, climate-friendly change in water and food sectors and market development in other sectors and value chains.
mineralScope: Not a named theme. The sustainable market development theme covers specific sectors and value chains linked to partner countries; whether any mineral chain qualifies is not established.
applicants: Partnerships of up to six partners led by an organisation with its registered office, or a branch, in the Netherlands; each must include a Dutch business and a local civil-society organisation, knowledge institution or business.
accessRoute: Application window expected from 7 December 2026 to 15 February 2027, according to the source. The source says it is temporarily closed until then.
whyItMatters: Included to show a common trap: a large, well-run programme with an upcoming window, but no stated mineral purpose.
notEstablished: That a mineral-related project would be eligible.

passages.quote: The minimum subsidy amount that can be applied for is 500,000 euros per application. The maximum is 3 million euros per application.

title: European Partnership for Responsible Minerals (EPRM)
summary: Multi-stakeholder partnership supporting responsible production at artisanal and small-scale mines in conflict-affected and high-risk areas, with project subsidies administered by RVO. Its last application window closed in November 2023.
objectives: Create better social and economic conditions for mine workers and local mining communities by increasing the number of mines that adopt responsible practices.
mineralScope: In 2023: tin, tantalum, tungsten, lithium, natural graphite, cobalt, copper and nickel.
period: Last application window: 1 September to 30 November 2023.
applicants: Members and project applicants subject to RVO's responsible business conduct guidelines; full eligibility is not reproduced here.
exclusions: Companies on UN or EU sanctions lists; activities on the FMO exclusion list.
accessRoute: None at present. The source says the programme is temporarily closed for application, with no reopening date.
whyItMatters: The clearest public funding precedent for artisanal and small-scale mining conditions linked to EU due-diligence rules.
notEstablished: Whether or when a new window will open. The page was last checked by RVO on 4 February 2026.

passages.quote: EPRM was established to create better social and economic conditions for mine workers and local mining communities.
In 2023, EPRM focuses on tin, tantalum, tungsten, lithium, natural graphite, cobalt, copper and nickel.

title: Extractives Global Programmatic Support (EGPS) Multi-Donor Trust Fund
summary: A World Bank multi-donor trust fund for the extractive sector. Recorded here through a disclosed grant for citizen engagement on accountability and transparency.
objectives: Not established from our sources beyond the disclosed award.
mineralScope: The extractive sector, which covers mining and also oil and gas.
accessRoute: Not established. The programme site refused automated requests when we checked.
whyItMatters: Trust funds like this are how several donors pool money that the World Bank then directs. The donors behind a grant are often invisible to the recipient's public.
notEstablished: The contributing donors, the size of the fund and any route for applicants.

title: Incentive Scheme to promote Critical Mineral Recycling (India)
summary: A ₹1,500 crore Government of India scheme of capital and operating subsidies for companies that recover critical minerals from e-waste, lithium-ion battery scrap and other scrap, over six years.
objectives: Develop recycling capacity in India for separating and producing critical minerals from secondary sources.
mineralScope: Critical minerals recovered from e-waste, lithium-ion battery scrap and other scrap such as catalytic converters.

perAward.display: ₹50 crore for large entities; ₹25 crore for small entities

applicants: Recycling companies that extract critical minerals, as defined in the scheme guidelines.
accessRoute: Through the Ministry of Mines scheme guidelines. Whether applications are currently accepted was not established from our sources.
whyItMatters: Puts public money into domestic recovery, which affects informal collectors and dismantlers upstream of the subsidised recyclers.
notEstablished: How the scheme treats informal workers in collection and dismantling, and how much has been disbursed.

passages.quote: total incentive (Capex plus Opex subsidy) per entity will be subject to an overall ceiling of Rs.50 crore for large entities and Rs.25 crore for small entities
a tenure of six years from FY 2025-26 to FY 2030-31
